title: Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Seat in Historic First
summary:
Mississippi has a new senator, and his win made history.

Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in a close race that took days of ballot counting to settle. Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, will become Mississippi's first Black U.S. senator since the years right after the Civil War, a time known as Reconstruction. That is a big deal in a state where white conservatives have held power for generations. The last time Mississippi voters picked a new Democratic senator was 1947, and the winner then supported segregation, the system that kept Black and white people apart by law.

Colom built his campaign around listening. "They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they're going through," he said in the final stretch of the campaign. He also said he could represent all of Mississippi, a state where race has long shaped politics and daily life. He talked about a party that represents rural America, suburban America and urban America, and that delivers for voters instead of offering excuses.

Colom's win adds to a set of midterm losses for President Donald Trump's party, which lost races in several states it usually controls. Democratic Senate leader Chuck Schumer celebrated the result online, writing that Colom "ran the campaign of a lifetime and re-imagined what's possible for Democrats in the South." Former President Bill Clinton and former Vice President Kamala Harris campaigned for Colom in the closing weeks. Colom is the son of a man who once worked for President Ronald Reagan as a Republican. When Trump held a rally for Hyde-Smith in Corinth, Mississippi, in late October, Colom walked along the line of Trump supporters waiting outside, introduced himself and asked about their concerns. Now he heads to Washington as Mississippi's next senator.
why_it_matters: A senator helps make the laws for the whole country, so who holds the seat matters to everyone in the state. Colom's win also shows how a state with a long history of racial division can change.

keywords.explanation: A prosecutor is a lawyer who brings cases against people accused of crimes.
Reconstruction was the time right after the Civil War when the country rebuilt and set new rules.
Segregation was a system of laws that kept Black and white people apart.
Conservatives are people who usually want to keep traditions and change things slowly.
A midterm election happens in the middle of a president's term to choose members of Congress and other offices.
A rally is a big public meeting where supporters gather to cheer for a candidate.

background_read: The U.S. Senate is one of the two houses of Congress, and each state elects two senators to make laws and vote on big decisions for the whole country.
After the Civil War ended slavery, the years called Reconstruction brought new rules and new rights, but many Southern states then passed laws that kept Black and white people apart.
For generations, white conservatives held most of the power in Mississippi, and race has shaped who wins elections and how people live.
In a midterm election, voters choose members of Congress and other offices in the middle of a president's term, and the results can show how the country feels about the party in power.
